title: Knowledge Enhanced Search Result Diversification

problem.claim: Search result diversification aims to reduce redundancy and improve subtopic richness for a query.

gap.claim: Existing approaches mainly measure document diversity from text or pre-trained representations, which may fail to capture some underlying query-document relationships.

contributions.claim: KEDIV uses knowledge-base entities and explicit relationships to model query-document relationships for search result diversification.
KEDIV builds a query-specific relation graph and applies a graph neural network with node-weight adjustment to produce context-aware entity and document representations at each selection step.
The approach derives diversity features from updated relation-graph node representations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on commonly used datasets show that KEDIV outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Search result diversification seeks less redundant and richer results.
Content-based and representation-based approaches may miss underlying query-document relationships.
KEDIV models these relationships with knowledge-base entities and a query-specific relation graph.
A graph neural network and node-weight adjustment produce context-aware representations used to derive diversity features.
The authors report improved performance over state-of-the-art methods on commonly used datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, or quantitative performance gains.
The abstract does not describe the knowledge base, graph construction details, node-weight adjustment algorithm, or computational cost.
The abstract does not report limitations, ablations, or independent verification.
